title: Quasi-coherent modules on an algebraic-space groupoid
statement: In the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $U,R$ algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $s,t:R\to U$, $e:U\to R$, $i:R\to R$ and $c:P\to R$, where $P$ with $p_0,p_1$ is the presheaf fibre product $R\times_{s,U,t}R$. Require the test-scheme groupoid laws [def-sfb-algebraic-space-groupoid], with $c(a,b)$ meaning first $b$, then $a$. A groupoid module is a quasi-coherent small-etale module $M$ on $U$ [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with an isomorphism $\alpha:t^*M\simeq s^*M$ for tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], satisfying $e^*\alpha=1$ and $c^*\alpha=p_1^*\alpha\circ p_0^*\alpha$. The identifications are the normalized tensor composition [def-sfb-space-module-tensor-composition] and identity [def-sfb-space-derived-pullback] comparisons. A morphism is an underlying module map $v:M\to N$ satisfying $t^*v;\beta=\alpha;s^*v$; identities and composition are those of module maps. The two forgetful functors take values in $\operatorname{QCoh}(U)$ and all small-etale module sheaves. Flatness of $s,t$ when imposed means chartwise flatness [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties].
